newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan rice exporters pin New Year hopes on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan rice exporters pin New Year hopes on Iraq.

text.p: Pakistani rice exporters have their sights set on Iraq, partly freed from the shackles of U.N. sanctions, as a new potential market in 1997.
"We are likely to export a substantial quantity of rice to Iraq in 1997," Javed Islam Agha, chairman of the Lahore-based Rice Exporters Association of Pakistan (REAP), told Reuters.
He gave no estimate, but one dealer said Pakistan might be able to sell up to half a million tonnes of rice to Baghdad.
"Pakistan could export about 500,000 tonnes of rice to Iraq in 1997," exporter Khalid Ghori of Matco Rice Processing said.
Dealers said Iraqi importers exploring the Pakistani rice market for the last two months would probably opt for IRRI-6 rice, cheaper than the basmati once favoured by Iraqi consumers.

The state-run Rice Export Corporation of Pakistan has invited bids by December 24 for the sale and export of 40,000 to 45,000 tonnes of IRRI-6 rice. "This will be a good chance for Iraq to buy rice in the auction," Agha said.

Prices rose to $550 per tonne FOB and $600 per tonne C&F following a demand for 9,000 tonnes of super basmati kernal variety brown (unpolished) rice from the 1996/97 (July-June) crop from a European country, Agha said.
REAP was working with the government and the RECP on a procedure to ensure that quality rice reached Europe, he said.
The REAP and the RECP would issue a certificate of quality and authenticity after an inspection and ask the exporter to pay a 3.0 percent guarantee to the government, Agha said.
"This is a good chance to establish the market for Pakistani rice in a European country," he added.

Rice exports rose 59 percent to 116,980 tonnes worth $35 million in November from 73,593 tonnes worth $25 million in October. July-November exports increased to 435,171 tonnes from 421,278 in the year-ago period.
A Karachi port official said at least 66,000 tonnes of rice had been booked for shipment to unidentified destinations in the first half of December.

Pakistan's rice output is expected to reach 3.5 million tonnes in 1996/97, slightly up on last year's 3.47 million. Production of IRRI-6 is estimated at 2.27 million tonnes and superior quality basmati at 1.2 million tonnes.
